title: How Your EV Makes Electricity When It Slows Down ⚡🛑 #shorts

scenes.text: Every time an electric car slows down, it can make electricity. How?
The motor works both ways. Send current in, and it turns the wheels. Let the wheels turn it, and it's a generator.
Making that current creates magnetic drag, which slows the car. The energy flows back into the battery instead of heating the brakes.
But it can't recover everything. Air and tire drag already used some energy, and each conversion loses a little as heat.
When the battery is full, too cold or too hot, the car cuts back regen to protect it, and the friction brakes take over.
That's why regen pays off most in stop and go city traffic.
Next time you lift off the pedal, you're charging. Could you drive with one pedal? Follow EV Drive for daily car tech.
